exposure: Magnetic-activated cell sorting (MACS) semen processing before ICSI
cohort: The study included 25,356 deliveries from ICSI cycles using donor oocytes and 19,703 deliveries from ICSI cycles using autologous oocytes, comparing those with standard semen preparation to those with an added MACS procedure.
finding: The use of MACS semen preparation before ICSI appears to be safe for mothers' and newborns' well-being, showing no significant differences in most obstetric and perinatal morbidities, a significant decrease in preterm birth for donor oocyte cycles, and an increase in gestational anaemia within general population prevalence.
